This is a claim petition under Section 166 r/w 140 of M.V. Act seeking claim in respect of death of
Sh.Ram Sewak s/o late Sh.Mool Chand in a road side accident stated to have taken place on
17.01.2017 near Hyundai Cut Chowki, Shalimar Garden, Ps Sahibabad, District Ghaziabad, Up.

It is
mentioned that on 17.01.2017 at about 11 p.m. deceased was driving his battery rickshaw
(e-rickshaw), along with his brother in law namely Pappu s/o Kanwar Pal and was duly observing
traffic rules and driving it at moderate speed.

It is stated that when e-rickshaw of the deceased
reached near Hyundai Cut chowki, Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad, suddenly a two wheeler/scooty
no.DL-5SAT-6636, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner by respondent no.1 hit
the e-rickshaw with great force, due to which deceased as well his brother in law fell on the road.
Deceased sustained multiple injuries.

Deceased was taken to hospital in Ghaziabad where he
succumbed to his injuries.

2. It is mentioned that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending
vehicle/scooty no.DL-5SAT-6636.

It is also stated that in respect of accident in question Fir

accident deceased was aged 42 years and was working as e-rickshaw driver and earning around

Petitioners were entirely dependent upon deceased being sole bread earner.

Issue No.1 10.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondent no.2/isurance on the other hand submitted that as per the post mortem report there was a crush injury on the head of the deceased due to which even brain material also came out.
It is submitted that such crush injury as described in PMR cannot occur by an accident of scooty.
It is submitted that the scooty has been falsely implicated in the case for making out a claim for compensation against the insurance.

It is further argued that evidence of PW2 also does not establish rash and negligent driving and involvement of vehicle no.
DL-5SAT-6636.

It is submitted that as per the cross examination of PW2 scooty hit the center portion of e-rickshaw from front side, due to which PW2 never received any injury whereas deceased received such big fatal injury, such aspect of the case is not at all believable that accident has been caused by scooty.
It is submitted that it came in the evidence that accident in fact was caused by one truck but later scooty was falsely implicated in this case.

13. Having considered the submissions at bar and taking note of the evidence on the record, first and foremost aspect to be noted is that PW2 in his affidavit stated that he was traveling with his brother in law/deceased in the e-rickshaw when it was hit by scooter no. DL-5SAT- 6636 resultantly his brother in law fell on the road and later succumbed to Digitally signed by MACT No.270/2017 Page 5 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.02.15 10:06:45 +0530 the injuries.

PW2 specifically stated that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 of scooty no.
DL-5SAT-6636.
Coming now to the cross examination of PW2, no doubt PW2 stated that scooty hit the e-rickshaw of the deceased from front and PW2 did not receive any injury.
It is also not disputed fact that as per PMR there was a crush injury on the head of the deceased which proved fatal.
Considering the nature of the injuries and the account of accident as given by PW2, no doubt certain doubts arise regarding the manner in which accident has taken place.
However nothing substantive came in the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve the substratum of the evidence of PW2 regarding accident.

Important in this context to note that in the entire cross examination of PW2 nowhere it is suggested either by respondent no.1 or by respondent no.2 that scooty in question was not involved in the accident.

14. It is matter of record that respondent no.1/driver has appeared in the witness box as R1W2 who in his examination in chief stated that no negligence can be attributed upon him for accident and that accident never occurred from his scooty.
However in cross examination R1W1 admits that he is facing the prosecution in criminal court regarding the accident in question.
He further admits that he has never made any complaint or representation to any higher authority of police or judiciary regarding alleged claim of being falsely implicated.

15. So far as regarding the nature of injuries mentioned in the PMR of deceased and involvement of scooty, it would be sufficient to say that neither respondent no.1 nor respondent no.2/insurance summoned the doctor who conducted the post mortem to clarify on this aspect as to whether such crush injury could be caused by an accident from scooty.

Thus,
for the reasons discussed above and the material available on record, this Tribunal concludes that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle/scooty bearing registration no.DL-5SAT-6636 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 16. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 17.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Ram Sewak.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in Digitally signed by MACT No.270/2017 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 8 MALIK Date:
2024.02.15 10:07:12 +0530 life and economic factors
, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.

Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

18. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-

Age of deceased :
19.
The petitioner no.1 Smt.Maya (PW1) in her evidence has placed on record documents of criminal case Ex.PW1/1 (colly.) in which age of deceased is mentioned to be 42 years.
Even there is no dispute with regard to age of deceased.
These documents in the opinion of this Tribunal are conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (17.01.2017) was about 42 years.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
20.
Petitioner no.1 Smt.Maya (PW1) in her deposition stated that MACT No.270/2017

During cross- examination PW1 stated that she has not filed any document to show that owner of battery rickshaw which was taken by her husband on rent.
PW1 also stated that she has not filed any document to show that her husband was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
21. No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month at the time of his death.

In the absence of any such material this Tribunal assesses income of deceased to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,214.12 per month.

22.
As held above, deceased was about 42 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

opennyai_summary.facts: No evidence was led on behalf of respondent no.2/insurance company.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
Considering the nature of the injuries and the account of accident as given by PW2, no doubt certain doubts arise regarding the manner in which accident has taken place.
However nothing substantive came in the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve the substratum of the evidence of PW2 regarding accident.
Important in this context to note that in the entire cross examination of PW2 nowhere it is suggested either by respondent no.1 or by respondent no.2 that scooty in question was not involved in the accident.
14. It is matter of record that respondent no.1/driver has appeared in the witness box as R1W2 who in his examination in chief stated that no negligence can be attributed upon him for accident and that accident never occurred from his scooty.
This Tribunal cannot assume that the nature of injury is such that it could MACT No.270/2017 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:

As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in Digitally signed by MACT No.270/2017 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 8 MALIK Date:
In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month at the time of his death.
In the absence of any such material this Tribunal assesses income of deceased to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,214.12 per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
27.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Since, the deceased was survived by three dependents, one-third of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on SHAILENDER MALIK MACT No.270/2017 MALIK Date: Page 12 2024.02.15 10:07:49 +0530 account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Since, the deceased was survived by three legal heirs, therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (48,000 X 3 + 18,000 + 18,000) under this head.
